subject.title: fix: block unresolved Telegram reply targets

question: Should unresolved Telegram reply targets be represented by a generic typed reply-context status from the Telegram plugin, or should core permanently recognize Telegram’s placeholder string?
rationale: The current patch works for one observed string, but choosing the permanent owner and contract affects the channel/plugin boundary and coordination with the structured reply-context work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90745.

options.title: Use plugin-owned typed status
options.body: Have Telegram parse rich messages or mark the target unresolved, then make core apply a channel-agnostic clarification gate.

options.title: Accept the narrow core guard
options.body: Land the exact Telegram string check as a temporary exception, accepting coupling and follow-up migration debt.

options.title: Coordinate with runtime-context PR
options.body: Pause this PR until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90745 establishes the reply metadata contract, then add unresolved status there.

recommendation.title: Use plugin-owned typed status
recommendation.body: Have Telegram parse rich messages or mark the target unresolved, then make core apply a channel-agnostic clarification gate.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available owner-side candidate from the recently shipped Telegram rich-message work.
